correctness.rationale: B=<2> modulo 73 has nine elements, its 9*8 ordered nonzero differences fill 1..72 exactly. Its affine stabilizer consists of nine multipliers in B and no nonzero translation, yielding 72*73/9=584 distinct orbit images. The affine signature of A is (0,1,3,7); exactly nine of B's 126 four-subsets have this signature and each is 2^j A; A has trivial affine stabilizer. Therefore exactly nine affine maps whose image contains A, constituting just one distinct B image after dividing by 9. An independent integer implementation exhaustively generated the 584 orbit images and directly found exactly one containing A. The implication for EVERY perfect difference set additionally and explicitly uses Hall/Niu classification of all cyclic (73,9,1) sets as this orbit; the finite orbit calculation does not prove that classification independently.
residual_risks: Global all-PDS statement depends on correct external cyclic projective-plane classification, not an independent census of all 73 choose 9 subsets.
No claim of uniqueness for different modulus or other four-subsets.

value.rationale: The seed {1,2,4,8} is the natural powers-of-two four-term example central to the Sidon-extension question; deciding whether the exhibited order-eight PDS completion is unique is a canonical rigidity question about a nonarbitrary seed. The exact one-completion result is not mechanically determined by PDS existence or total orbit size and can inform extension/counterexample studies. Its finite specificity and dependence on a known classification are material qualifications, not automatic worthlessness.
residual_risks: No general all-moduli extension theorem or classification of all seed types.

final_claim: For the four-term Sidon seed A={1,2,4,8} in Z/73, B={1,2,4,8,16,32,37,55,64} is the unique cyclic (73,9,1) perfect difference set containing A, assuming the published complete affine-orbit classification; the Singer affine orbit has 584 sets, and only B contains A.
limitations: Covers fixed modulus 73 and fixed seed A; no statement about other moduli.
